digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate / acceptance criteria quality (P6 DET floor)
propositions: AC items carrying operational-evidence markers (deploy, prod, live-run, IaC-apply, cloud-state, merge-gate, human-action, drill, store-surgery, recorded-attestation) but lacking [operator-attested] tag are not flagged until retroactively tagged, causing plan-review close-gate cycle failures (cases 115b, 8c4f).
A deterministic, lexicon-based advisory lint (extending p6_ac_quality, never blocking) flags untagged operational-evidence ACs at plan time to surface the tagging gap before claim submission.

The lint is implemented as a pure helper function in det_operator_attested.py (single source of truth for _OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE shared with workflow_ops) and integrated into p6_ac_quality with precision ≥70% and flag rate ≤5% over the historical AC corpus.
Both known failure cases (tickets 115b and 8c4f) fire on their historical AC text when the tag is stripped, and already-tagged items do not fire, verified by unit test fixtures.

The lint ships advisory and prompt-less in the packaged floor without adding a new P-level, modifying DET_CHECKS cardinality, or changing criteria_routing.json; commits are ordered so the deterministic self-gate eval precedes lint activation in git ancestry.
